# Spar 0.4.0

Spar 0.4 turns the existing coding workspace into a persistent adaptive training system.

## What changed

- Today is now the primary experience, with one persisted recommendation, its training intent, source, target ability, and an inspectable “Why this?” explanation.
- Tracks are living goals over one global learner model, not isolated courses or fixed syllabi.
- The learner model now separates proficiency from confidence and retains linked evidence, recency, trend, training status, readable memory, and next-verification intent.
- Mistakes move through observation, hypothesis, pattern, monitoring, and resolved states. Spar cannot promote a pattern until linked evidence spans independent attempts.
- Progress adds a provisional evidence-based Spar Rating, rating history, active training, strengths, uncertain abilities, patterns, notices, and detailed ability timelines.
- History remains the durable account of what happened, including source, outcome, assistance, attempts, runs, replacements, and full challenge timelines.
- Onboarding and Today now support adaptive baseline calibration. Imported provider history contributes context but direct calibration remains distinct.
- Settings now uses a native-style section sidebar and keeps raw learner state, decisions, patterns, evidence, baseline, rating, and engine metadata inside Advanced / Learning Engine.

The local execution environment, LeetCode and Codeforces integrations, generated challenges, mutable challenge flow, attempt telemetry, ability ledger, and primary Training Agent remain the underlying execution system.
